# @zakkster/lite-utils

Seven standalone CLIs: six bash tools that compare two JavaScript builds through V8's own
traces -- bytecode length, deopts, inline caches, inlining decisions, young-GC
event counts, object shapes / elements kinds / field generalizations -- and end every run with a fail-closed verdict line
(SAME / DIFF / NO-VERDICT, or WITHIN / OVER, ZERO / NONZERO, REPORTED). Each
bash tool is one self-contained script that drives `node` and reads its trace
output. The seventh, `alloc-per-op`, is a node script that measures steady-state
on-heap bytes per op of a synchronous lane (PASS / FAIL, SAME / DIFF, NO VERDICT).
This is not a JS library: no JS API is supported (alloc-per-op.mjs's exports serve its tests and carry no contract).

## Status

Version 1.2.1 (2026-11-28), on npm as @zakkster/lite-utils (1.0.0, 2026-11-12, was the first release).

Install (instructions; pick one):

- `npm i -D @zakkster/lite-utils`
- `npm i -D git+https://github.com/PeshoVurtoleta/lite-utils.git`
- copy ONE root script into your project and run it with `bash <script>` (alloc-per-op: `node alloc-per-op.mjs`); a
  root never sources or imports another package file at run time.

After an npm install the commands are in `./node_modules/.bin/`:
`allocation-diff`, `alloc-per-op`, `bytecode-budget`, `deopt-diff`, `ic-diff`,
`inlining-budget-diff`, `shape-diff`.

## Rules for a caller (read first)

- ALWAYS require the `VERDICT <v>` line on stdout, not only the exit code (the six bash tools;
  `alloc-per-op` prints no `VERDICT` line: use its exit code, 0 / 1 / 2, or `--json`).
- Exit 2 = NO-VERDICT: the tool could not decide and failed closed. It is not
  "no difference". Never treat 2 as success.
- Exit 0 and 1 are verdicts; the verdict word names which (see each tool).
- `--self-test` exit 1 means a `FAIL <label>` line was printed (alloc-per-op: a row printed `MISS`; its exit 2 = a
  selfCheck miss). It is NOT DIFF.
- `-h` / `--help` prints the header and exits 2 (all seven). Do not use it as a
  liveness probe that expects 0.
- An unexpected failure inside a tool exits 2 NO-VERDICT, never 1.
- A refused argument exits 2 before any node is spawned, with these named
  exceptions: a `--v8-flags` flag outside the allowlist is refused after one
  `node --v8-options` read; ibd refuses some mode errors after its probes.
- An unknown option exits 2 with a did-you-mean hint.

## Tools

Shared options (each tool's own `-h` is the authority for its subset):
`--node BIN` (default `$NODE`, else `node`; resolved once to an absolute
path), `--v8-flags STR` (runtime allowlist of V8 flags; log / trace / print /
prof flags and node options are refused), `--out DIR` (keep the report and raw
runs), `--runs N` (runs per side; run 1 vs the later runs is the null control; with --zero: young 0 vs young >= 1 per run),
`--self-test`, `-h`. The six bash tools strip NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_V8_COVERAGE,
NODE_COMPILE_CACHE and NODE_REDIRECT_WARNINGS from every spawn (alloc-per-op's one --expose-gc respawn inherits the
environment).

### bytecode-budget (bytecode-budget.sh)

Question: how many bytes of bytecode does each NAMED function compile to?

    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER                                 # report
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --max fn=N[,fn=N] --node-version vX.Y.Z DRIVER   # gate
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --diff --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER      # diff
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --diff --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before-ref REF --after-ref REF --module REL   # diff, ref mode
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --diff --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before FILE --after FILE                      # diff, file mode

- Report: exit 0 REPORTED, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- Gate: `--max` limits plus `--node-version` (required; must equal
  `<node> --version` exactly, else NO-VERDICT). Per function WITHIN / OVER;
  exit 0 WITHIN, 1 OVER, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- Diff: compares the length multisets of two drivers (or two staged module
  versions in ref / file mode); exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. `--max` is
  refused with `--diff`.
- Ref / file mode needs git. In file mode the "before" file must be a frozen
  copy, not a git-tracked file.
- Tier: DETERMINISTIC on one node binary and one driver; any run-to-run change
  is NO-VERDICT, never OVER or DIFF. The limit values the tool prints are that
  binary's, a measurement of that binary, not a law. Maxima are only valid on
  the node version they were recorded on.

### deopt-diff (deopt-diff.sh)

Question: did the deoptimizations of NAMED functions change (code tier, kind,
reason, as a multiset)?

    deopt-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER                                  # driver mode
    deopt-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before-ref REF --after-ref REF --module REL   # ref mode
    deopt-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before FILE --after FILE                     # file mode
    deopt-diff.sh --self-test [--fixtures DIR]

- Exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. `--fn` is required.
- A "Tier" section after the function lines is REPORTED and never moves the
  verdict or exit code.
- Tier: the verdict on a user driver is STATISTICAL (deopts follow tier-up
  timing). `--self-test`, `--self-test --fixtures DIR` and the natives pair
  (deopt.mjs vs mono.mjs) are DETERMINISTIC.

### ic-diff (ic-diff.sh)

Question: did the inline-cache states (kind, key, final state) of NAMED
functions change?

    ic-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER
    ic-diff.sh --self-test

- Driver mode ONLY. There is no ref mode and no file mode.
- Exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- On node 22 and 24 this tool always ends NO-VERDICT (by design; see Known
  limits). V8 15.6 (node 27 alpha) shares the V8 14.x numbering: verdicts
  there (#128).
- Tier: the verdict on a user driver is STATISTICAL; `--self-test` is
  DETERMINISTIC.

### inlining-budget-diff (inlining-budget-diff.sh)

Question: did the TurboFan / Maglev inlining DECISIONS for NAMED functions
change, plus a budget report?

    ME=m0 inlining-budget-diff.sh [opts] DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER      # driver mode (any project)
    inlining-budget-diff.sh [opts] --before-ref REF --after-ref REF       # lite-signal: builds from git refs
    inlining-budget-diff.sh [opts] --before FILE --after FILE             # lite-signal: two Signal.js files

- Driver mode is the general one (function names from `--fn` or `$ME`).
  The ref and file modes are lite-signal-shaped: they expect Signal.js /
  Watch.js and a driver importing `./Signal.js`. Do not use them on other
  projects.
- Options specific to it: `--fn LIST`, `--tiers LIST` (`turbo`, `maglev`),
  `--only-fn`, `--concurrent`, `--driver FILE`, `--repo DIR`,
  `--no-bytecode`. Output goes to `--out DIR` (default `$OUTDIR`, else a
  timestamped dir under `$TMPDIR`); a rerun needs a fresh, new or empty
  `--out`.
- Verdict per tier: exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. The budget report is
  REPORTED and never moves the verdict.
- Node 22: the maglev tier is NO-VERDICT; use `--tiers turbo`.
- Tier: the verdict is STATISTICAL, the budget report is REPORTED. There is no
  live control in the test suite; only `--self-test` (canned trace text) is
  deterministic.

### allocation-diff (allocation-diff.sh)

Question: did the number of young-generation GC EVENTS inside a marked window
change? Counts of GC events, never bytes.

    allocation-diff.sh [opts] DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER     # diff: SAME / DIFF
    allocation-diff.sh [opts] --zero DRIVER                  # gate: ZERO / NONZERO
    allocation-diff.sh --self-test

- Diff mode only plus `--zero`; no ref mode and no file mode.
- Exit 0 SAME or ZERO, 1 DIFF or NONZERO, 2 NO-VERDICT. With --zero a young GC in every run is NONZERO even when
  the counts differ from run to run (`NONZERO -- young GC(s) in the window in every run (young per run <y1>,<y2>,..)`);
  a young GC in some runs only is NO-VERDICT (`null control: run k differs from run 1 (--zero: run 1 young a | run k young b)`).
- A GC that the V8 stack guard runs at the guard's hand-over can read
  `trace lost 1 GC line in run k (guard count c, trace c-1)`: NO-VERDICT
  (exit 2, fail closed), rare (0 natural hits locally; CI sightings: LEDGER #138),
  window unaffected.
- ZERO means less than one semi-space of young allocation in the
  window, not zero bytes. An allocation TurboFan scalar-replaces is not an
  allocation: ZERO is then the correct reading.
- Driver contract: mark the window with
  `fs.writeSync(1, '@@LITE-MARK start\n')` and the same for `end`, written
  synchronously, before exit. Never use console.log or process.stdout in the
  driver. Warm up before `start`; a cold window over-reports.
- Tier: the script logic is DETERMINISTIC (`--self-test`); a verdict on a user
  driver is STATISTICAL and REPORTED only.

### shape-diff (shape-diff.sh)

Question: did the shape instability of NAMED functions change (object shapes / maps, elements kinds, field
generalizations, as multisets)? Attributed per function; unattributed instability is checked as a whole.

    shape-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER
    shape-diff.sh --self-test

- Driver mode ONLY. There is no ref mode, no file mode and no `--stable` mode (LEDGER #145). `--fn` is required (short
  function names; `--fn=LIST` also works).
- Options specific to it: `--include-transitions` (put normal monomorphic Transition / InitialMap counts into the
  verdict; by default they are REPORTED and never move it), `--runs N` (2..20, default 3), `--out DIR` (keeps
  `DIR/report.txt` and `DIR/raw/<side>/run.<k>.{log,out}`). `--v8-flags` also refuses any flag whose name contains
  `sparkplug`, `concurrent-recompilation` or `stress-concurrent-inlining` (the tool pins them; message `shape-diff:
  --v8-flags must not set <flag>: conflicts with ...`), exit 2.
- CLI: an empty value for any value option (`--fn`, `--runs`, `--node`, `--v8-flags`, `--out`) is refused at its argv
  position (`<opt> must not be empty`). `--runs` takes 1-2 decimal digits (`09` is 9; `024` is refused in your
  spelling). An unknown option gets a did-you-mean hint (`--outt` -> `(did you mean --out?)`).
- Exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. Precedence over every function: NO-VERDICT > DIFF > SAME. DIFF: the attributed shape-instability multiset differs for >= 1 target
  function. SAME needs identical attributed multisets AND identical unattributed / non-target multisets.
  NO-VERDICT: a refusal, a parse error, a failed null control (run 1 vs the later runs), missing execution evidence, a
  target Transition whose map has no map-details line (elements kind unknown), or unattributed / external
  instability (`Reflect.deleteProperty`, `splice`, a non-target user helper, a `node:` or other non-file-path frame)
  that changed while the attributed sites looked SAME, or "tier-up differs (optimized-frame key set)" / "tier-up
  differs (interpreted key set)" while the interpreted multisets are equal. A changed unattributed delta never becomes
  DIFF; the line names its owner (`user:<fn>`, `node:<fn>`, `Builtin:*`, `other:<fn>`, `NONE`). A DIFF report also
  prints a differing unattributed delta (REPORTED; the verdict stays DIFF).
- Classes: a ReplaceDescriptors map line is MAP_REPLACE for every reason, target and non-target, except a
  reason-MapCreate line whose (owner, source site) has exactly 1 hit in a run: it is not counted (the literal-map cache
  fill; execution evidence is kept); >= 2 hits count. A target `[reconfiguring]` line is a RECONF verdict record, so a
  changed one reads DIFF. `map-move` lines (GC compaction) are followed, not refused (a malformed one is NO-VERDICT
  `map-move does not parse`; `--stress-compaction` runs are readable). A `--fn` name defined at >1 location in a run
  reads NO-VERDICT "ambiguous target function".
- `--include-transitions` advice: a constructor field add, or a `push` that moves the elements kind, can read SAME /
  NO-VERDICT in default mode; check a field-added commit with `--include-transitions`.
- **Blind spot: a single cold call to `Array.prototype.push(1.5)` emits 0 trace lines, so two drivers that differ only
  by that call read SAME. Warm the function (e.g. 200 calls) or compare with another tool. Measured on darwin arm64,
  node v22.23.5 / v24.22.3 / v26.8.2 / v27.0.0-alpha.0.1.0 (REPORTED; LEDGER #146).**
- Evidence guard: a function with no optimizing compile and no attributed map / shape event in a run (a clean array or
  arithmetic function, or compiled but never called) reads NO-VERDICT; warm up so it tiers up, e.g. 20000 calls
  (nominal; one research run on v26.8.2, not reproduced). The call count at which a helper inlines can differ from a
  default-tier run (LEDGER #146).
- Node: needs node >= 22; an unparsable `--version` or a major below 22 exits 2 after the one `--version` spawn,
  before `--v8-options` and before any write. The tool traces with `--log-maps --trace-elements-transitions
  --trace-generalization --no-sparkplug --no-concurrent-recompilation --no-concurrent-sparkplug --no-node-snapshot`,
  not node's default tier config.
- Refusal label: a CR / LF in an option name is refused with the label `option name` (the other bash tools say
  `unknown option`). A symlink `--out` dir (a trailing `/` or `/.` is stripped first, so `lnk/` is refused; a deeper
  `lnk/sub/..` is not checked: not a security boundary), a symlink or hard-linked `DIR/report.txt`, a
  non-empty `DIR/raw`, a driver that is `DIR/report.txt`, and an empty `--fn` are refused before any spawn.
- No `@@LITE-MARK` window is used or needed; the driver runs whole.
- Tier: `--self-test` is DETERMINISTIC (58 rows, a fake node, no real node; rows 41-44 replay captured excerpts of
  real node 22 / 24 / 26 / 27 and expect DIFF with the removed map record named, Point SAME; rows 45-53 are the
  audit-fix rows, row 54 the interpreted key set, rows 55-58 MapCreate single-hit and map-move). A shape-diff verdict on a
  real node is REPORTED only (no statistical gate). REPORTED: shape-probe run 45521613713 on b07e739 (run-probes.sh against the research prototype, not the shipped
  root), 27 / 27 ok on
  11 / 11 runs (ubuntu node 22 / 24 / 26 x default GNU Awk 5.3.2 / gawk / mawk 1.3.4; macOS node 26 x BSD awk / gawk;
  one dispatch). The default-tier A/B of the research prototype, not the shipped root (node 24.22.3 / 26.8.2, darwin arm64, one run, 2026-11-24) read SAME; the A/B
  does not cover verdicts with user code in a Sparkplug frame (see Known limits).

### alloc-per-op (alloc-per-op.mjs)

Question: how many ON-HEAP BYTES does one op of a synchronous lane allocate, steady state, in the main isolate?

    alloc-per-op [opts] [--max B] BENCH           # table, or gate: PASS / FAIL / NO VERDICT
    alloc-per-op [opts] --tol B BENCH_A BENCH_B   # A/B: SAME / DIFF / NO VERDICT
    alloc-per-op --self-test [--json]

- BENCH: an ES module exporting `lanes`, a plain object of synchronous functions `lane(i)`; an optional exported
  `setup()` (plain or async; a generator is refused, exit 2) is awaited once, before `lanes` is read. A bench that
  imports the tool file again inside its run is refused. Example: `const sink = [{}, {}]; export const lanes = { 'name': (i) => { sink[i & 1] = i + 0.5; } };`
- Options: `--n` 100000..100000000 (default 1000000), `--windows` 3..50 (default 5; PEAK = max of windows 1..K-1),
  `--warm` (default 200000), `--sub` 1000..10000 (default 10000; N % S == 0, N / S <= 10000), `--lane NAME`
  (repeatable), `--max B`, `--tol B` (required in A/B), `--json` (the last line the tool writes to stdout). Option
  checks run before any spawn, except a `--lane NAME` (checked after the bench loads, setup() has run; a dash-led NAME
  is a name).
- lane(i): i runs 0 .. S-1 in every sub-window and restarts; it is not an op index. An allocation that needs i >= S
  never happens; one at i = 0 happens once per sub-window. A GC inside a sub-window VOIDs it: a lane allocating more
  than new space holds per sub-window (on the order of 100 B/op at the default S; it depends on the new-space size) is
  NO VERDICT, never FAIL; lower --sub.
- Exit 0 PASS / SAME / table; 1 FAIL / DIFF / ONLY-A / ONLY-B; 2 NO VERDICT or refused. `--self-test`: 0 all rows ok,
  1 a row missed, 2 the selfCheck missed. Output has a `gate --max ...` / `A/B --tol ...` line, no `VERDICT` line.
- Refusal band: lo = 32 / S, hi = hiFixed + 0.001 x peak, hiFixed = 524288 / N, doubled below --n 1000000
  (PRELIMINARY). A `--max` below lo, or a `--tol` below lo + hiFixed, is refused before any spawn (corner --tol floor
  at --n 100000 --sub 10000: 10.48896). The floor (empty lane) is printed and never subtracted; null after a selfCheck
  miss. A rejected sub-window is retried (at most 3): a retry calls the lane again. The same path twice as A and B (after realpath) is refused; a hard link or a case variant counts as a copy.
- Scope: on-heap bytes, main isolate. Reads new_space, old_space, large_object_space, new_large_object_space;
  code_space and trusted_space count into old_space, code_large_object_space and trusted_large_object_space into
  large_object_space; read_only_space and the shared spaces are not read. Off-heap ArrayBuffer memory and Worker
  threads are not counted (no Worker detector); lite-perf-gate's arrayBuffers signal covers external memory.
- The lane must STORE what it allocates: a dropped allocation (returned, or discarded in the body, e.g.
  `(i) => { add(A, B); }`) may be elided by V8 and then reads 0 B/op. A lane that returns a value is refused, but only
  lane(0)'s return value is checked, so a value or a thenable from a later call is not seen. An allocation that does not
  recur inside the span ((K-1) x N ops) is seen only if an occurrence falls inside it, by every rule. The default `--warm` covers constructor, class-field and literal shapes. `--sub` below
  1000 under-reads on node v22. A bench that replaces v8.GCProfiler gets a fence miss, exit 2: at import or in setup() a selfCheck miss (no lane
  measured); in a lane, every lane verdict NO VERDICT (`fence (after)`). A
  prototype patch of v8.GCProfiler / v8.getHeapSpaceStatistics, or a swap restored before the run ends, is not detected.
  On a fence miss a non-VOID gate text lane line ends ` (fence)` (A/B text lines: no label); every lane verdict in --json is NO VERDICT. A table run's NO VERDICT is exit 2 plus the stderr line (no verdict field in --json). The tool exits when the event loop
  drains: a bench that leaves a timer, socket or Worker open keeps it running; a signal to the tool alone does not reach
  the --expose-gc child it re-spawns (signal the process group).
  `--no-concurrent-recompilation` lowers noise; it is not forced. A threshold holds only for the build it was measured
  on (pointer compression, arch, node / v8).
- Tier: `--self-test` rows DETERMINISTIC (untimed, in CI); a verdict on a user lane STATISTICAL. Numeric constants
  FROZEN by S-A36 (CI run 43691163080, at --n 1e6 / 1e7 x --sub 1e3 / 1e4; the --n 1e5 / 1e8 corners rest on local
  PRELIMINARY data only); read set and driver re-frozen by S-A51 (CI run 44945969102); both REPORTED tier (hosted CI,
  one run each). Needs node only (no bash, no awk).

## Exit codes and the VERDICT line

| tool                  | 0                  | 1                 | 2          |
|-----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|------------|
| bytecode-budget       | WITHIN / REPORTED / SAME | OVER / DIFF | NO-VERDICT |
| deopt-diff            | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| ic-diff               | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| inlining-budget-diff  | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| allocation-diff       | SAME / ZERO        | DIFF / NONZERO    | NO-VERDICT |
| shape-diff            | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| alloc-per-op          | PASS / SAME / table | FAIL / DIFF / ONLY-A / ONLY-B | NO VERDICT / refused |

For the six bash tools: every run that reaches a verdict ends in a `VERDICT <v>` line on stdout; a refusal prints
`<tool>: <why>` and `VERDICT NO-VERDICT` on stderr and exits 2; a SIGINT /
SIGTERM / SIGHUP during a run ends NO-VERDICT, exit 2; `--self-test` exits 0 (all checks ok) or 1 (a FAIL line), and
that 1 is not DIFF. alloc-per-op: a refusal prints `alloc-per-op: <why>` only; its exits are in its row above and its
section. `-h` exits 2 (all seven).

## Tiers

- DETERMINISTIC: same inputs give the same verdict. bytecode-budget (one node
  binary), each tool's `--self-test`, the deopt-diff natives pair.
- STATISTICAL: the verdict on a user driver follows warm-up, GC and tier-up
  timing (deopt-diff, ic-diff, inlining-budget-diff, allocation-diff, alloc-per-op). Run
  them on a quiet host. Their verdict on a user driver is a report, not a build gate (alloc-per-op --max and
  allocation-diff --zero still exit 1 on FAIL / NONZERO).
- REPORTED: printed measurements that gate nothing (inlining budget report,
  deopt-diff tier section, allocation-diff counts line). A shape-diff verdict on a real node is REPORTED
  (its `--self-test` is DETERMINISTIC).

## Requirements

- bash >= 3.2 (the six bash tools; alloc-per-op needs only node).
- A POSIX awk (BSD awk and the ubuntu-latest awk are what the CI matrix uses;
  other awks are not claimed).
- node >= 22, with the ic-diff and inlining-budget-diff caveats above.
- git, for ref and file modes.
- `sha256sum` or `shasum`.
- No runtime npm dependencies.

## Known limits

Each bullet names its LEDGER id.

- an inherited SHELLOPTS=noexec runs nothing and exits 0; callers must require the VERDICT line, not only the exit code
  (#124)
- #66: `--v8-flags` numeric values are checked for FORM only; a value such as `=NaN` passes the check, node then fails,
  and the tool ends NO-VERDICT.
- #83: ic-diff on node 22 and 24 ends NO-VERDICT; a NO-VERDICT, never a wrong verdict. V8 15.6 (node 27 alpha) uses
  the V8 14.x numbering, so it gives verdicts (#128).
- #122: a refusal may print a name that git, readlink or a PATH lookup resolved; a CR or newline in it (behind a
  symlink with a clean name, or in a PATH directory) reaches stderr inside that refusal; exit 2.
- #84: allocation-diff does not strip NODE_NO_WARNINGS (it strips four other names); it can move the GC count.
- #76 (1), #80: inlining-budget-diff leaves its `--out` contents behind after some refusals; a rerun needs a fresh
  `--out`.
- #123: inlining-budget-diff file mode decides its "byte-identical, null control" NOTE on Signal.js alone; a differing
  Watch.js can print that NOTE and then DIFF. The verdict is right, the NOTE is false.
- alloc-per-op: the lane must STORE what it allocates (a dropped allocation may be elided by V8 and then reads 0 B/op);
  only lane(0)'s return value is checked (a value or a thenable from a later call is not seen); off-heap ArrayBuffer
  memory and Worker threads are not counted; an allocation that does not recur inside the span ((K-1) x N ops) is seen
  only if an occurrence falls inside it, by every rule.
- #146: shape-diff cannot see a single cold `Array.prototype.push(1.5)` call (0 trace lines; two drivers that differ
  only by it read SAME); two `del` helpers in different files share one owner key, so instability moving between them
  reads SAME (not probed); a function with no optimizing compile and no attributed event reads NO-VERDICT until
  warmed; a V8 trace-format change (renamed or suppressed prefixes) can blind it; it traces with `--no-sparkplug
  --no-node-snapshot` (a default-tier A/B of the research prototype, not the shipped root, on node 24 / 26 darwin arm64
  changed no verdict, but no user function ran in a Sparkplug frame there, so verdicts with user code in baseline frames
  are not covered).
  Real-code limits (#146, #153; REPORTED, 5 suite packages, node v26.8.2 / v26.3.1; all fail closed):
  - `--fn <Class>` on a class with instance or static fields (private fields and `static {}` included) reads
    NO-VERDICT "ambiguous target function": V8 logs each field initializer under the class name at the field line. A
    class expression escapes. Target the methods, not the class.
  - An added or removed NON-target class with fields reads NO-VERDICT (each field declaration adds a 1-hit top-level
    CopyAddDescriptor MAP_REPLACE line per run, counted as non-target instability); a field-less class reads SAME.
  - Two same-name functions (a registry method plus a module wrapper) read "ambiguous target function" once both
    compile; an arrow assigned as `read.set = (value) => ...` gets the inferred name `read.set`, which `--fn`
    refuses, so such code is only ever unattributed. UNATTR GEN counts are trace lines (one event is 2 lines);
    attributed sites dedupe; verdicts are unaffected.
  - node v26.8.2 sometimes drops elements-transition lines (a LiteSignal null control: NO-VERDICT in 3 of 10 runs).
  - A constructor field add, or a push that moves the elements kind, reads SAME / NO-VERDICT in default mode: use
    `--include-transitions`. A deopt loop with no shape event reads SAME (use deopt-diff).
  - The GEN key includes the `(+N maps)` count, so a changed count alone reads DIFF.
  - A directory name that looks like a frame bracket (`a) [x+1 at y/`) can still be mis-split (documented, not fixed).
- #147: the no-op filter for a generalization line with identical representations is closed by M2a (a `(+N maps)` line
  is not a no-op; a target `[reconfiguring]` line is a RECONF verdict record). A back-pointer-less attribute
  reconfigure normalizes (MAP_NORMALIZE, NO-VERDICT, fail-closed); that path is UNVERIFIED.
- Driver output is trusted (#72 B1b, #92 b): a driver can write lines that look like trace or marker output.
- a hard link to `--before` elsewhere in the repository (outside `--before`'s directory and below), or under a case-only
  sibling name on a case-sensitive file system, can stay undetected (LEDGER #71, #88, #89)
- Not a security boundary: the argument refusals are fail-closed hygiene, not a sandbox.

## Composability

One CI job can run all seven (alloc-per-op: `node alloc-per-op.mjs --self-test`, untimed, in CI; installed:
`./node_modules/.bin/alloc-per-op --max B bench.mjs`). Gate only on bytecode-budget `--max` (exit 1 or 2 fails the job).
Run the five other bash tools so a nonzero exit does not abort the job, keep `--out` as an artifact, and fail the job if
the `VERDICT` line is missing:

    rc=0; ./node_modules/.bin/deopt-diff --fn add --out out/dd before.js after.js > dd.txt || rc=$?
    grep -q '^VERDICT ' dd.txt || exit 1

A statistical verdict is a report, not a build gate. Call installed tools as
`./node_modules/.bin/<name>`.
